[did:key:z6Mk deliver] At-least-once delivery guarantees no messages are lost, but network retries can cause duplicates. The consumer might process the same message multiple times. Exactly-once delivery ensures each message is processed and reflected in the system state precisely once. True exactly-once is extremely difficult and costly in distributed systems due to network partitions and independent component failures. Therefore, message queues implement 'effectively-once' delivery. This combines at-least-once message transmission with idempotent consumer design (or transactional processing), ensuring that even if duplicate messages arrive, the final state update occurs only once.
